ai.title: Chemotherapy Mechanisms
ai.subject: Pharmacology
ai.summary: Chemotherapy drugs target rapidly dividing cells by interfering with DNA replication, mitotic spindle formation, or cell‑cycle checkpoints. Understanding these mechanisms helps predict efficacy, toxicity, and resistance patterns.

sections.p: Chemotherapy uses cytotoxic agents to kill or halt the growth of malignant cells. The drugs act on cellular processes that are more active in cancer cells than in normal tissues, but some normal cells (e.g., bone marrow, GI mucosa) are also affected.
The therapeutic window is narrow; dose intensity must be balanced against cumulative toxicity. Resistance can arise from drug efflux, DNA repair, or altered drug targets.

sections.p: In low‑resource settings, drug availability, monitoring capacity, and supportive care differ. Clinicians must choose regimens with manageable toxicity and consider local infections that may complicate therapy.
